---
process: release
title: Production release
category: Releases
group: Engineering / Releases
tags: production, deploy
owner: person-casey
backup: person-avery
context: ticket, commit, environment, tag
roles: release-lead, qa, backend
---

## Before production changes · DO-CONFIRM {#prep}
- [!] {change.request} Change request approved for tonight's window @release-lead {#approved}
  system: Change board
  window: The release window on the ticket
  require: number
- [!] {ci.gate} Full test gate green on the release commit ^commit {#tests}
  pipeline: web-app gate
  page: https://ci.example.com/job/web-app-gate/
  require: run
  > Run the gate **after** the rebase. A green run on an earlier commit doesn't count.
- [!] {confirm} Feature flags set in the deploy values ^environment @backend {#flags}
  > New features ship off. Turn them on in the environment's values file, never in code.
- [!] {confirm} Rollback commit written in the release ticket @release-lead {#rollback}
- [ ] {run.process} Check in the release notes for this commit @release-lead {#notes}
  process: check-in
  carry: commit
  > Starts a linked check-in run. This step is checked when that run completes.
- [ ] {communicate} Post "starting release" in the team channel @release-lead {#announce}
  channel: #team-releases
  message: Starting the production release of ^commit (^ticket). I'll post again when it's verified.

## Gate: Ready to deploy · owner @release-lead {#ready}
  approves: deploy of `^commit` to ^environment

## Deploy · READ-DO {#deploy}
- [!] {bitbucket.pr} Merge the release branch to master ^commit @release-lead {#merge}
  action: merge
  repo: web-app
  from: release
  to: master
  require: all
  sets: tag
  > Merging to master **is** the production release. Rebase first; never merge commits into the branch. The merge creates the release tag; record it here and every later step uses it.
- [!] {jenkins.job} Start the production deploy job ^tag @backend {#jenkins}
  job: web-app-deploy-prod
  parameters: TICKET=^ticket TAG=^tag
  stage: Stage 5 asks for the release ticket number
  require: build
  expect: 25m
  after: 2h
  > The job stops at stage 5 and asks for the release ticket number. Type it exactly as it appears in Jira.
- [!] {ui.action} Approve the deploy in Jenkins before it rolls back @release-lead {#approve}
  system: Jenkins
  deadline: external
  > Jenkins rolls the deploy back if nobody approves within 30 minutes. Copy its deadline into Flightdeck with **Set deadline** so everyone sees the countdown.
- [!] {run.command} New pods stay up with no restarts @backend {#pods}
  command: kubectl get pods -l app=web-app
  where: Your terminal
  expected: RESTARTS is 0 for every new pod after 20 minutes
  expect: 20m

## Gate: Deployed · owner @release-lead {#deployed}
  approves: `^commit` running in ^environment

## Verify in production · READ-DO {#verify}
### Track: Product checks @qa {#checks}
- [!] {confirm} Smoke prompts return their expected answers @qa {#smoke}
  where: Release ticket, "Smoke prompts" section
  evidence: note
- [ ] {verify.health} No new error events on the logs dashboard @qa {#logs}
  dashboard: https://logs.example.com/d/web-app-errors
  metric: New error events
  threshold: None that weren't there before the release
  watch: 30m
### Track: Wrap-up @release-lead {#wrap}
- [ ] {communicate} Post the result in the team channel @release-lead {#result}
  channel: #team-releases
  message: ^tag (^commit) is live in ^environment and verified. Thanks, everyone.
- [ ] {deploy} Deploy record shows ^tag in ^environment @release-lead {#deploy-record}
  environment: ^environment
  artifact: web-app
  version: ^tag
  tool: https://deploy.example.com/apps/web-app
  rollback: The rollback commit in the release ticket
  > The Jenkins job does the deploy. This step records what actually landed, so the receipt says which version went out and when.
- [ ] {jira.issue} Close the release ticket @release-lead {#close}
  action: transition
  issue: ^ticket
  issueType: Release
  status: Done

release.brief:
# Create a skill from Production release v1

Build a skill that does this whole process of the team's process "release", exactly as the published checklist says.
Store the skill wherever the team keeps it, then register it in the team folder as `skills/<name>.json` with `"implements": "release@1"`, its own `"version"` and its `"location"` (the skill's source path or link: a repo, a shared folder or a local path).

## Run details it receives

- ticket
- commit
- environment
- tag

## The process, in order

### Phase: Before production changes (DO-CONFIRM: do the work, then confirm each step)
- **approved** {change.request} Change request approved for tonight's window (must do)
  - evidence: Change number (number, text, required); Change link (link, url)
  - system: Change board
  - window: The release window on the ticket
  - require: number
  - who: release-lead
- **tests** {ci.gate} Full test gate green on the release commit (must do)
  - evidence: Run number (run, text, required); Run link (runLink, url)
  - pipeline: web-app gate
  - page: https://ci.example.com/job/web-app-gate/
  - require: run
  - tied to run details: ^commit (if one changes, the step must be redone)
  - note: Run the gate **after** the rebase. A green run on an earlier commit doesn't count.
- **flags** {confirm} Feature flags set in the deploy values (must do)
  - who: backend
  - tied to run details: ^environment (if one changes, the step must be redone)
  - note: New features ship off. Turn them on in the environment's values file, never in code.
- **rollback** {confirm} Rollback commit written in the release ticket (must do)
  - who: release-lead
- **notes** {run.process} Check in the release notes for this commit
  - process: check-in
  - carry: commit
  - who: release-lead
  - note: Starts a linked check-in run. This step is checked when that run completes.
- **announce** {communicate} Post "starting release" in the team channel
  - evidence: Link to the message (sent, url)
  - channel: #team-releases
  - message: Starting the production release of ^commit (^ticket). I'll post again when it's verified.
  - who: release-lead
**Gate: Ready to deploy** (owner: release-lead), approves deploy of `^commit` to ^environment. Stop here until a person passes it; never pass it for them.

### Phase: Deploy (READ-DO: read each step, then do it, in order)
- **merge** {bitbucket.pr} Merge the release branch to master (must do)
  - evidence: Pull request link (pr, url, required); Merge commit (mergeCommit, text, required)
  - action: merge
  - repo: web-app
  - from: release
  - to: master
  - require: all
  - sets: tag
  - who: release-lead
  - tied to run details: ^commit (if one changes, the step must be redone)
  - note: Merging to master **is** the production release. Rebase first; never merge commits into the branch. The merge creates the release tag; record it here and every later step uses it.
- **jenkins** {jenkins.job} Start the production deploy job (must do)
  - evidence: Build number (build, text, required); Build link (buildLink, url)
  - job: web-app-deploy-prod
  - parameters: TICKET=^ticket TAG=^tag
  - stage: Stage 5 asks for the release ticket number
  - require: build
  - expect: 25m
  - after: 2h
  - who: backend
  - tied to run details: ^tag (if one changes, the step must be redone)
  - note: The job stops at stage 5 and asks for the release ticket number. Type it exactly as it appears in Jira.
- **approve** {ui.action} Approve the deploy in Jenkins before it rolls back (must do)
  - evidence: Reference (ID or link) (reference, text)
  - system: Jenkins
  - deadline: external
  - who: release-lead
  - note: Jenkins rolls the deploy back if nobody approves within 30 minutes. Copy its deadline into Flightdeck with **Set deadline** so everyone sees the countdown.
- **pods** {run.command} New pods stay up with no restarts (must do)
  - evidence: What you saw (result, text, long text)
  - command: kubectl get pods -l app=web-app
  - where: Your terminal
  - expected: RESTARTS is 0 for every new pod after 20 minutes
  - expect: 20m
  - who: backend
**Gate: Deployed** (owner: release-lead), approves `^commit` running in ^environment. Stop here until a person passes it; never pass it for them.

### Phase: Verify in production (READ-DO: read each step, then do it, in order)
Track "Product checks" (qa), in parallel with the phase's other tracks:
- **smoke** {confirm} Smoke prompts return their expected answers (must do)
  - evidence: What you saw (evidence, text, long text, required)
  - where: Release ticket, "Smoke prompts" section
  - evidence: note
  - who: qa
- **logs** {verify.health} No new error events on the logs dashboard
  - evidence: Result (result, choice: one of Pass / Fail); Value you saw (observed, text); Screenshot or link (snapshot, url)
  - dashboard: https://logs.example.com/d/web-app-errors
  - metric: New error events
  - threshold: None that weren't there before the release
  - watch: 30m
  - who: qa
Track "Wrap-up" (release-lead), in parallel with the phase's other tracks:
- **result** {communicate} Post the result in the team channel
  - evidence: Link to the message (sent, url)
  - channel: #team-releases
  - message: ^tag (^commit) is live in ^environment and verified. Thanks, everyone.
  - who: release-lead
- **deploy-record** {deploy} Deploy record shows in
  - evidence: Version deployed (deployed, text); Deploy link (deployLink, url); Finished at (finished, text)
  - environment: ^environment
  - artifact: web-app
  - version: ^tag
  - tool: https://deploy.example.com/apps/web-app
  - rollback: The rollback commit in the release ticket
  - who: release-lead
  - tied to run details: ^tag, ^environment (if one changes, the step must be redone)
  - note: The Jenkins job does the deploy. This step records what actually landed, so the receipt says which version went out and when.
- **close** {jira.issue} Close the release ticket
  - action: transition
  - issue: ^ticket
  - issueType: Release
  - status: Done
  - who: release-lead
**Gate: confirm "Verify in production" together**. Stop here until a person passes it; never pass it for them.


## Evidence from runs

0 completed runs on this version, 0 clean (none).

## Rules

- Do only what the steps say; where a step is done by hand in a tool, have the skill stop and ask.
- Never put secrets, tokens or customer data in the skill.

sprint-start.brief:
# Create a skill from Start a sprint v1

Build a skill that does this whole process of the team's process "sprint-start", exactly as the published checklist says.
Store the skill wherever the team keeps it, then register it in the team folder as `skills/<name>.json` with `"implements": "sprint-start@1"`, its own `"version"` and its `"location"` (the skill's source path or link: a repo, a shared folder or a local path).

## Run details it receives

- sprint
- capacity

## The process, in order

### Phase: Before planning (DO-CONFIRM: do the work, then confirm each step)
- **close-last** {jira.sprint} Last sprint closed in Jira (must do)
  - evidence: Sprint link (sprintLink, url); Issues carried over (carriedOver, text)
  - action: close
  - board: Web app board
  - sprint: The active sprint
  - who: scrum-lead
- **carryover** {jira.sprint} Unfinished stories moved to the new sprint or the backlog
  - evidence: Sprint link (sprintLink, url); Issues moved (moved, text)
  - action: move-incomplete
  - board: Web app board
  - sprint: The sprint just closed
  - who: scrum-lead
- **velocity** {measure} Velocity of the last sprint recorded
  - evidence: Value (value, text); Unit (unit, text)
  - metric: Story points completed in the last sprint
  - unit: points
  - where: Jira velocity chart
  - who: scrum-lead
- **carried-points** {measure} Points carried over from the last sprint
  - evidence: Value (value, text); Unit (unit, text)
  - metric: Story points of the unfinished stories
  - unit: points
  - who: scrum-lead
- **capacity** {confirm} Capacity for the next two weeks in person-days, after time off (from the team calendar)
  - sets: capacity
  - who: scrum-lead
- **roadmap** {ui.action} Sprint dates copied into the team roadmap
  - evidence: Reference (ID or link) (reference, text)
  - system: Team roadmap
  - who: scrum-lead
**Gate: confirm "Before planning" together**. Stop here until a person passes it; never pass it for them.

### Phase: Planning (READ-DO: read each step, then do it, in order)
- **meeting** {meeting} Sprint planning with the whole team, sized to person-days (must do)
  - evidence: Outcome (outcome, text, long text)
  - attendees: Everyone
  - at: 10:00
  - who: scrum-lead
  - tied to run details: ^capacity (if one changes, the step must be redone)
- **goal** {confirm} Sprint goal agreed as one sentence (must do)
  - evidence: What you saw (evidence, text, long text, required)
  - evidence: note
- **criteria** {confirm} Every committed story has acceptance criteria (must do)
**Gate: Sprint ready** (owner: scrum-lead), approves ^sprint. Due by 12:00. Stop here until a person passes it; never pass it for them.

### Phase: After planning (DO-CONFIRM: do the work, then confirm each step)
- **start** {jira.sprint} Sprint started in Jira (must do)
  - evidence: Sprint link (sprintLink, url); Sprint name (name, text); Sprint dates (dates, text)
  - action: start
  - board: Web app board
  - sprint: ^sprint
  - who: scrum-lead
  - tied to run details: ^sprint (if one changes, the step must be redone)
- **set-goal** {jira.sprint} Sprint goal set in Jira
  - evidence: Sprint link (sprintLink, url)
  - action: set-goal
  - board: Web app board
  - sprint: ^sprint
  - goal: The goal agreed in planning
  - who: scrum-lead
- **post** {communicate} Goal posted in the team channel
  - evidence: Link to the message (sent, url)
  - channel: #team
  - who: scrum-lead
**Gate: confirm "After planning" together**. Stop here until a person passes it; never pass it for them.

0 completed runs on this version, 0 clean (none).

## Rules

- Do only what the steps say; where a step is done by hand in a tool, have the skill stop and ask.
- Never put secrets, tokens or customer data in the skill.
